sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: A month after sending the National Guard into Washington to fight crime there,
sentences.zh: 在向华盛顿派遣国民警卫队打击犯罪一个月后，

sentences.en: President Trump is so pleased with the results that he's now discussing how to put federal troops onto the streets of cities across the country, from Chicago to New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统对结果非常满意，他现在正在讨论如何将联邦军队部署到全国各地的城市街道上，从芝加哥到新奥尔良。

sentences.en: It's a potentially dramatic expansion of what has already become an unprecedented military deployment on domestic soil.
sentences.zh: 这可能会使已经在国内领土上达到前所未有的军事部署规模进一步戏剧性地扩大。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Jessica Chung speaks with residents of Washington about what it's really like when the National Guard comes to town.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事杰西卡·钟将采访华盛顿居民，了解国民警卫队进驻后，他们的真实感受。

sentences.en: It's Monday, September 8th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月8日，星期一。

sentences.en: I'm announcing a historic action to rescue our nation's capital from crime, bloodshed, bedlam, and squalor, and worse.
sentences.zh: 我宣布采取一项历史性行动，将我们的首都从犯罪、流血、混乱、肮脏以及更糟糕的情况中拯救出来。

sentences.en: Our capital city has been overtaken by violent gangs and bloodthirsty criminals, roving mobs of wild youth, drugged-out maniacs and homeless people,
sentences.zh: 我们的首都已被暴力团伙、嗜血罪犯、横行霸道的野蛮青年、吸毒成瘾的狂徒和无家可归者所占领，

sentences.en: and we're not going to let it happen anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会再让这种情况发生。

sentences.en: We're not going to take it.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不容忍。

sentences.en: This is Liberation Day in D.C., and we're going to take our capital back.
sentences.zh: 这是华盛顿特区的解放日，我们要夺回我们的首都。

sentences.en: We're taking it back.
sentences.zh: 我们要把它夺回来。

sentences.en: A day after President Donald Trump announced he was deploying National Guard troops into Washington, D.C., the first Humvees started pulling in.
sentences.zh: 在唐纳德·特朗普总统宣布向华盛顿特区部署国民警卫队的一天后，第一批悍马车开始驶入。

sentences.en: They lined up between the African American History Museum and the Holocaust Museum along the National Mall.
sentences.zh: 它们沿着国家广场，在非裔美国人历史博物馆和犹太大屠杀纪念馆之间排成一列。

sentences.en: About 800 troops eventually came, and they weren't alone.
sentences.zh: 最终大约有800名士兵抵达，而且他们并不孤单。

sentences.en: President Trump also called on the DEA, Homeland Security, and the FBI.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统还召集了缉毒局、国土安全部和联邦调查局。

sentences.en: My message to residents is this.
sentences.zh: 我给居民们的信息是这样的。

sentences.en: We know that access to our democracy is tenuous.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，我们对民主的参与是脆弱的。

sentences.en: D.C.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿特区。

sentences.en: Mayor Amir O'Bowser complied with all of this, saying there wasn't much you could do, which makes sense.
sentences.zh: 市长阿米尔·奥鲍泽对此表示顺从，称你对此无能为力，这倒也说得通。

sentences.en: The city is a federal district where the president controls the National Guard.
sentences.zh: 这座城市是一个联邦特区，总统掌控着国民警卫队。

sentences.en: And while this action today is unsettlingly and unprecedented,
sentences.zh: 虽然今天的行动令人不安且史无前例，

sentences.en: I can't say that given some of the rhetoric of the past, that we're totally surprised.
sentences.zh: 但考虑到过去的一些言论，我不能说我们完全感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Violent crime in Washington is actually falling, dramatically.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿的暴力犯罪实际上正在急剧下降。

sentences.en: Some people found all of this strange.
sentences.zh: 有些人觉得这一切很奇怪。

sentences.en: Crime in D.C.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿特区的犯罪率

sentences.en: has actually dropped to a 30-year low.
sentences.zh: 实际上已经降至30年来的最低点。

sentences.en: Let's look at some of this data.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看这些数据。
2023年，华盛顿特区

sentences.en: had its most murders in more than two decades, 274.
sentences.zh: 发生了274起谋杀案，是二十多年来最多的一年。

sentences.en: But it then plunged to 187 murders last year, and it's been falling again so far this year.
sentences.zh: 但去年骤降至187起，今年到目前为止还在持续下降。

sentences.en: So there is no crime emergency.
sentences.zh: 所以根本不存在犯罪紧急状态。

sentences.en: So it's hard to say exactly what the purpose is.
sentences.zh: 因此很难说其目的究竟是什么。

sentences.en: You think it's really about crime?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这真的是为了打击犯罪吗？

sentences.en: This is not about crime.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是为了犯罪问题。

sentences.en: This is about control.
sentences.zh: 这是为了控制。

sentences.en: So people were resistant.
sentences.zh: 所以人们对此感到抵触。

sentences.en: This is not about public safety.
sentences.zh: 这与公共安全无关。

sentences.en: This is about power.
sentences.zh: 这是为了权力。

sentences.en: A Washington Post poll found that 8 out of 10 residents were against the federal takeover of law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 《华盛顿邮报》的一项民意调查发现，十分之八的居民反对联邦接管执法权。

sentences.en: Who's city?
sentences.zh: 这是谁的城市？

sentences.en: Our city.
sentences.zh: 我们的城市。

sentences.en: Who's city?
sentences.zh: 这是谁的城市？

sentences.en: Our city.
sentences.zh: 我们的城市。

sentences.en: Who's city?
sentences.zh: 这是谁的城市？

sentences.en: To Americans who don't live in D.C., you think of the landmarks.
sentences.zh: 对于不住在华盛顿特区的美国人来说，你们想到的是那些地标。

sentences.en: The White House, the monument, the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 白宫、纪念碑、国会大厦。

sentences.en: But to locals, they think of their city in terms of four quadrants.
sentences.zh: 但对当地人来说，他们眼中的城市分为四个象限。

sentences.en: Northeast, northwest, southwest, and lastly, southeast, where crime is the higheSt.
sentences.zh: 东北、西北、西南，最后是犯罪率最高的东南区。

sentences.en: So we wanted to talk to people living there, to know what they thought about this, how life has changed since the feds came to town.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想和住在那里的人谈谈，了解他们的想法，以及联邦人员进驻后生活发生了怎样的变化。

sentences.en: And they told me the streets are quieter, which is quite a change compared to what it's normally like,
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我街道变安静了，与往常相比确实变化很大，

sentences.en: especially in one of the most dangerous neighborhoods in southeast, Congress Heights.
sentences.zh: 特别是在东南区最危险的社区之一，国会高地。

sentences.en: When you walk into Congress Park, the tension is high.
sentences.zh: 当你走进国会公园时，气氛非常紧张。

sentences.en: Every day, all day, you can feel the tension.
sentences.zh: 每天，整天，你都能感受到那种紧张感。

sentences.en: Shootings all the time.
sentences.zh: 枪击事件不断。

sentences.en: I hear gunshots all day long.
sentences.zh: 我整天都能听到枪声。

sentences.en: There are young guys killing each other.
sentences.zh: 有年轻人在互相残杀。

sentences.en: Child got killed.
sentences.zh: 孩子被杀了。

sentences.en: She got shot riding a scooter.
sentences.zh: 她骑着滑板车时被枪击中。

sentences.en: It's trouble.
sentences.zh: 这真是麻烦。

sentences.en: We talked to two residents who work in neighborhood safety.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了两位从事社区安全工作的居民。

sentences.en: I drive to the doctor's office, and it's a shame that when you get in your car, you can't sit there like you used to, because somebody will carjack you.
sentences.zh: 我开车去医生办公室，真丢人，当你坐进车里时，你不能像以前那样安稳地坐着，因为随时会有人劫车。

sentences.en: So you just get in your car, lock the doors, and pull off.
sentences.zh: 所以你只能赶紧上车，锁好车门，然后开走。

sentences.en: It's a loving community.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满爱的社区。

sentences.en: It's just trauma-filled.
sentences.zh: 只是充满了创伤。

sentences.en: So in a split second, it can go from loving to violent, you know what I mean, and a heartbeat.
sentences.zh: 所以在一瞬间，它可能从充满爱变成暴力，你明白我的意思吗，就在心跳之间。

sentences.en: And it's just taking our lives away from us.
sentences.zh: 这简直是在夺走我们的生活。

sentences.en: It's almost like we're in prison.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像我们身处监狱一样。

sentences.en: Sondra Seegers was one of the people we talked to.
sentences.zh: 桑德拉·西格斯是我们采访的对象之一。

sentences.en: She grew up in D.C.
sentences.zh: 她在华盛顿特区长大，

sentences.en: and lives in Congress Heights.
sentences.zh: 住在国会高地。

sentences.en: Sondra is 74 years old.
sentences.zh: 桑德拉今年74岁。

sentences.en: She lives in a small brick house with manicured rose bushes and hydrangeas.
sentences.zh: 她住在一栋带修剪整齐的玫瑰丛和绣球花的小砖房里。

sentences.en: My block, we keep the grass cut.
sentences.zh: 我们这一片，草坪都修剪得很整齐。

sentences.en: She's a community activiSt.
sentences.zh: 她是一位社区活动家。

sentences.en: Seven years ago, she founded a local group called Crave, Concerned Residents Against Violence.
sentences.zh: 七年前，她创立了一个名为Crave的当地组织，即“关注暴力问题的居民”。

sentences.en: They lobby the city to spend more money on safety in her ward.
sentences.zh: 他们游说市政府在她的选区投入更多资金用于安全保障。

sentences.en: When she hears that crime is at a low point in the city, even in her neighborhood, it doesn't feel that way to her.
sentences.zh: 当她听说城市的犯罪率处于低点，甚至在她的社区也是如此时，她并没有这种感觉。

sentences.en: How do you react to people who say, actually, crime is down, and that people did try to stop the crime, and it was successful?
sentences.zh: 对于那些说“实际上犯罪率下降了，人们确实努力阻止了犯罪，而且很成功”的人，你有什么回应？

sentences.en: Every other night, I can look down the street and see— She says the crime problem in Congress Heights goes back decades.
sentences.zh: 每隔一天，我往街上看就能看到——她说国会高地的犯罪问题由来已久。

sentences.en: Her own brother was shot and killed in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 她自己的兄弟在70年代被枪杀。

sentences.en: But she says back then, crime was targeted toward people who were involved in it.
sentences.zh: 但她说那时候，犯罪是有针对性的，针对的是那些卷入其中的人。

sentences.en: And for the most part, bystanders were left alone.
sentences.zh: 而且在大多数情况下，旁观者是安全的。

sentences.en: And as time went on, things changed.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，情况发生了变化。

sentences.en: There was more crime.
sentences.zh: 犯罪变多了。

sentences.en: The store shut down.
sentences.zh: 商店关门了。

sentences.en: But now, especially since the pandemic, she says it feels like the violence is more random.
sentences.zh: 但现在，特别是在疫情之后，她说感觉暴力变得更加随机了。

sentences.en: And for Sondra, that means more innocent people and even businesses are caught up in it.
sentences.zh: 对桑德拉来说，这意味着更多无辜的人甚至企业被卷入其中。

sentences.en: She points to a nearby storefront that can't seem to stay open.
sentences.zh: 她指着附近一家似乎无法维持营业的店面。

sentences.en: She says after the murder of George Floyd, the police were too lenient on crime.
sentences.zh: 她说在乔治·弗洛伊德被谋杀后，警察对犯罪太宽容了。

sentences.en: She was also frustrated with the D.C.
sentences.zh: 她还对华盛顿特区的一项法律感到沮丧，

sentences.en: law that prevented kids from being charged with adult crimes.
sentences.zh: 该法律禁止以成年人罪名起诉未成年人。

sentences.en: She was so fed up that she actually wrote a letter to the mayor and city council asking for the National Guard to be sent in.
sentences.zh: 她实在忍无可忍，甚至写信给市长和市议会，要求派遣国民警卫队。

sentences.en: And she wasn't alone.
sentences.zh: 而且她并不孤单。

sentences.en: The ward's council member, Trayon White, did too.
sentences.zh: 该选区的议员特雷翁·怀特也这么做了。

sentences.en: But their response was no.
sentences.zh: 但他们的回应是否定的。

sentences.en: So Sondra, too afraid to go outside, hasn't been to a grocery store in two years.
sentences.zh: 所以桑德拉因为太害怕而不敢出门，已经两年没去过杂货店了。

sentences.en: I'm announcing a historic action to rescue our nation's capital from crime, bloodshed, bedlam.
sentences.zh: 我宣布采取一项历史性行动，将我们的首都从犯罪、流血、混乱中拯救出来。

sentences.en: She was listening to the local radio station one late afternoon when she heard the president describe the city as one beset by crime and lawlessness.
sentences.zh: 那天傍晚，她正在听当地广播电台，听到总统将这座城市描述为一个饱受犯罪和无法无天困扰的地方。

sentences.en: But you want to have safety in the streets.
sentences.zh: 但你想要街道安全。

sentences.en: You want to be able to leave your apartment or your house.
sentences.zh: 你想要能够离开你的公寓或房子。

sentences.en: It resonated with her.
sentences.zh: 这引起了她的共鸣。

sentences.en: I did not vote for Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我没有投票给唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: I did not.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: And I don't agree with a lot of things he's doing.
sentences.zh: 而且我不同意他做的很多事情。

sentences.en: But when he decided to bring in the National Guard and the federal agencies, I was happy.
sentences.zh: 但当他决定引入国民警卫队和联邦机构时，我很高兴。

sentences.en: It was announced that same night that I didn't hear gunshots, no shootings and no stabbing.
sentences.zh: 就在那天晚上，我没听到枪声，没有枪击，也没有刺伤事件。

sentences.en: I saw one car come by and one person walking, and that was it.
sentences.zh: 我只看到一辆车经过，一个人走过，仅此而已。

sentences.en: People calmed down.
sentences.zh: 人们平静下来了。

sentences.en: She has yet to see federal agents in her neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 她还没有在她的社区看到联邦特工。

sentences.en: But she says that her neighbors have.
sentences.zh: 但她说她的邻居们看到了。

sentences.en: One of them sent her a video from his porch surveillance camera.
sentences.zh: 其中一位邻居从他门廊的监控摄像头给她发了一段视频。

sentences.en: It shows a trail of 12 unmarked cars going down an alleyway.
sentences.zh: 视频显示一串12辆无标记的车辆驶入了一条小巷。

sentences.en: And she said that many of her neighbors feel the same as her.
sentences.zh: 她说她的许多邻居和她有同样的感受。

sentences.en: Nelson's trying to stop the criminals.
sentences.zh: 尼尔森正在努力阻止罪犯。

sentences.en: And we all suffer.
sentences.zh: 而我们都在受苦。

sentences.en: So with him, he's serious about it.
sentences.zh: 所以对于他，他是认真的。

sentences.en: As for the people in D.C.
sentences.zh: 至于华盛顿特区那些不同意她的人，

sentences.en: who don't agree with her, who want them out,
sentences.zh: 那些想要他们离开的人，

sentences.en: Sondra says they're protesting the wrong thing.
sentences.zh: 桑德拉说他们抗议的对象错了。

sentences.en: Where were they when these children, babies, and toddlers were getting murdered?
sentences.zh: 当这些孩子、婴儿和幼儿被谋杀时，他们在哪儿？

sentences.en: Where were they then?
sentences.zh: 那时候他们在干什么？

sentences.en: They didn't protest anything.
sentences.zh: 他们什么都没抗议。

sentences.en: But now they're protesting.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们却在抗议。

sentences.en: Here's somebody trying to make it safer for us.
sentences.zh: 这里有人试图让我们更安全。

sentences.en: They're protesting now.
sentences.zh: 他们现在却在抗议。

sentences.en: Delusional.
sentences.zh: 简直是妄想。

sentences.en: Sondra says she still doesn't venture too far from home.
sentences.zh: 桑德拉说她仍然不敢离家太远。

sentences.en: But she now feels like she doesn't have to worry as much.
sentences.zh: 但她现在觉得不用那么担心了。

sentences.en: I don't be watching my back like I used to.
sentences.zh: 我不用像以前那样时刻提防着背后了。

sentences.en: I just go out and be pulling the weeds from my flowers.
sentences.zh: 我只是出去拔拔花草。

sentences.en: I feel safe.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很安全。

sentences.en: Nah, what they're doing is putting a temporary fix on a bigger issue.
sentences.zh: 不，他们所做的是给一个更大的问题打了一剂临时补丁。

sentences.en: Not everyone in Congress Heights feels this way.
sentences.zh: 并非所有国会高地的居民都这么想。

sentences.en: I believe it's a show.
sentences.zh: 我认为这只是一场秀。

sentences.en: Three blocks over, Levon Williams, a D.C.
sentences.zh: 在三个街区外，华盛顿特区本地人莱冯·威廉姆斯（Levon Williams），

sentences.en: native, works in a nearby neighborhood complex as a violence interrupter for a local nonprofit.
sentences.zh: 在附近的一个社区综合体工作，担任当地一家非营利组织的暴力调解员。

sentences.en: His target area is Congress Park.
sentences.zh: 他的目标区域是国会公园（Congress Park）。

sentences.en: Say two neighborhoods are beefing, getting into a shooting at each other.
sentences.zh: 比方说两个社区之间有矛盾，发生了枪击冲突。

sentences.en: So I go to one neighborhood first, speak to who I'm, you know, the lead is in that neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 我会先去其中一个社区，和我知道的那个社区的负责人谈谈。

sentences.en: Then I go to the other neighborhood, do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 然后我去另一个社区，做同样的事情。

sentences.en: Bring the two neighborhoods together and I mediate the conflict.
sentences.zh: 把两个社区的人聚在一起，由我来调解矛盾。

sentences.en: Levon is trained in this line of work.
sentences.zh: 莱冯受过这方面的工作培训。

sentences.en: Mental health and behavior training.
sentences.zh: 接受过心理健康和行为方面的训练。

sentences.en: But he also says that he can do this because he has established credibility within the neighborhood.

sentences.en: When we asked the Department of Homeland Security about what Christopher and his dad told us, they refuted their account.

sentences.en: They said ICE agents clearly identify themselves as law enforcement, including by wearing the proper identifying clothing.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，ICE特工会明确表明自己的执法身份，包括穿着适当的识别服装。

sentences.en: They also said that their agents are trained to ask a series of questions to determine a person's status and if arrests needed, to use the minimum possible force.
sentences.zh: 他们还称，他们的特工受过训练，会通过一系列问题来确定一个人的身份，如果需要逮捕，会使用尽可能最小的武力。

sentences.en: And lastly, they denied the conditions in Chantilly, saying that detainees have access to phones, legal representation, and three meals a day.

sentences.en: Their goal, they said, is to support, quote, the reestablishment of law and order and public safety so Americans can feel safe in our nation's capital.
sentences.zh: 他们说，他们的目标是支持所谓的“重建法律与秩序和公共安全”，这样美国人才能在我们的首都感到安全。

sentences.en: Even though Christopher got his dad back, things feel different now.

sentences.en: Very worried that it could happen again.
